messages:
eli: Quick sync — intake boundary for model onboarding. Proposal: split ingest into a very fast "smoke" gate and a separate full "bench" gate. Smoke should catch obvious ABI/signature and runtime crashes in <30s, bench can run longer perf/quality sweeps. Thoughts?
sara: strong +1. our current pipeline blocks on bench and it slows ad-hoc uploads a lot. smoke-first would help iter iteration speed.
aj: agree but need clear contract for what smoke guarantees. do we require kv-cache warmup? or just inference sanity?
maria: my take: smoke = surface-level checks: model loads, tokenization sanity, minimal sample generation, and signature compatibility. no long perf runs, no full evals. bench = perf + regression suites + golden outputs.
drew: edge: if smoke is too permissive we push flaky models downstream. suggest smoke include a small set of deterministic seeds and a checksum on model files. also fail fast on obvious quantization mismatches.
ben: +1 to deterministic seeds. For ABI/signature, we should embed a tiny manifest in the model tar: `onboard.yaml` with `input_schema`, `kv_cache_supported: true/false`, `quant_profile`. intake-bot: automated check suggestion: compute model fingerprint, validate manifest present, run `smoke_infer` container with `--timeout 25s`.
eli: example manifest snippet I had in mind:
```
name: my-model
version: 1.0
input_schema: {type: string, encoding: utf8}
outputs: [text]
kv_cache_supported: true
compat_level: basic
```
sara: compat_level field is nice — allows us to route to different runtime paths and fallbacks. basic vs runtime-optimized vs experimental.
aj: routing is key. can we attach compat_level as metadata so serving can prefer a compatible variant? eg `compat_level: basic` => place on generic runtime, `optimized` => specialized kernels.
maria: for the bench gate we should require a signed manifest and a tiny contract test suite (jsonl) that the bench runner can execute. ranker/regression tests should be deltas vs golden.
drew: tradeoff: adding too many required artifacts raises onboarding friction. consider default shims: if manifest missing, smoke still runs with heuristics but marks `compat_level: inferred` and sets flag to require owner signoff before release.
ben: implementation note: intake-bot can auto-generate a `compat_hint` when it infers, and create a PR to the model registry metadata. owners can override.
eli: decision candidate: implement smoke gate with: (1) manifest presence check (soft fail -> inferred), (2) deterministic quick infer (3 seeds), (3) file fingerprint, (4) kv/quant quick check. Bench remains opt-in for dev uploads but required for production pinning.
sara: approve that flow. could we also add a knob to let platform teams require bench for certain teams or orgs?
aj: yes, policy layer should support `bench_required: true` per org. I can add that to policy service.
maria: action items: aj -> policy flag, ben -> intake-bot changes to infer manifest + fingerprint, drew -> small smoke test harness + default seeds, eli -> update onboarding docs and quickstart.
eli: cool — if no objections I'll open a follow-up RFC with the exact smoke contract and sample manifest schema. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
